⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **For the maintainer:** a re-ruling of #23556 / #23594 B (`{{object}} {{record}}` = object label + record **id**).
- **Options:**
  - **A, the record's title** (triage leaning). Use its `nameField`, as `ctx.title()` already resolves it, and fall back to the id only when no title exists: "Your Contract «Acme MSA 2026» was approved." **Workload:** S.
  - **B, keep the id.** Recipients cannot tell which record without opening it.
- **Lean: A.** Note the boundary: the title is shown only to recipients who are on the request, the same audience the id reaches today, so no new disclosure.

Brief-claimed-by: session_01KrKXQVvgYk2AJ4VkqMobyb · batch #402 · 2026-10-26T17:39Z

Director seat, summon #51 continuation (ledger objectstack#12708). Presented to the maintainer in batch #402 as item 2 of 2 (the two approvals cards filed from the hotclm browser regression thread). Seat increment (re-verified on `origin/main` `cdd4eea9`; the card and the triage leaning 6420598906 / 6420611091 are not restated):
- The standing ruling and its reason, read in code: `action-link-pages.ts:54–62` (#23594): "the record is named by its id, never by its title. A subject title is served only to a reader who may read the field it comes from, narrowed by that reader's field-level security … these pages have no reader to narrow for: the bearer carries a token, not a session"; `messages.ts:66–72` and `approval-notification-text.ts:64–84` build `{{object}} {{record}}` from the object label and the record id. So the id rule exists for a **reader-less** surface (email action-link pages read under the system context), and the triage line "same audience, no new disclosure" is incomplete: a title is a field, and a recipient's field-level security may hide it.
- Consequence for the letters: A is sound only as **A′ — per-recipient**: each notification is rendered for one recipient, so the title is resolved as that recipient (ADR-0079 `nameField`, narrowed by their FLS, id when empty or unreadable), while the token-bearing action-link pages keep the id (no reader to narrow for). That re-rules #23556 / #23594 B for notifications and leaves it standing for the action pages — the maintainer's call, which is why the card is in the box.
- Half-state read, not written: both decision-state labels together; the second leaves in the ruling's stroke.
- Facets (the card has no block; seat's reading): ① one naming rule, "the record's display name as the reader may see it", applied per surface by whether a reader exists — narrower than two rules by surface type; ② measured on hotclm: 7 of 11 notifications name a 16-character id, the app's own bell names the title; ③ per-recipient FLS narrowing fails closed to the id, never leaks a title; ④ no key, no gate.
- The seat agrees with **A′** (title per recipient, id fallback; action-link pages unchanged). Not B (title plus id on every line is noise once the title is right; keep the id only as the fallback) and not C. Workload: approvals lane · S (the subject-params resolver gains a per-recipient title read; messages unchanged in shape).
Prior rulings read: `#23594` · `#23556` · `{{record}}` → `action-link-pages.ts:54`, `messages.ts:28`; ADR-0079; thread: 6420611091.

Ruling: batch #402 item 2 · letter A′ · maintainer 「同意」 2026-10-26T23:00Z

Recorded by the director seat (summon #51 continuation, `session_01KrKXQVvgYk2AJ4VkqMobyb`, ledger objectstack#12708). The maintainer answered batch #402 with 「同意」 — both seat letters. Brief 6423124361. Letter **A′, the record's title per recipient**: an approval notification (the in-app bell row and the email body — every surface rendered for one named recipient) names the record by its display title (ADR-0079 `nameField`, resolved **as that recipient** and narrowed by their field-level security), falling back to the record id when the title is empty or unreadable to them. The token-bearing action-link pages (`action-link-pages.ts:54–62`, read under the system context with no reader to narrow for) keep naming the record by object label and id — the #23594 reason stands there. This re-rules #23556 / #23594 letter B for the notification surfaces only; the maintainer's acceptance is the re-ruling. Not B (title plus id on every line; the id is the fallback, not a suffix) and not C.

Workload of the chosen letter (card column): approvals lane · S — `subjectParams` / `approval-notification-text.ts:64–84` gains a per-recipient title read reusing the request page's existing title resolution (`ctx.title()` / `nameField`), the message templates keep their `{{object}} {{record}}` shape, one test per fallback (empty title; title field unreadable to the recipient), and a dated note beside the #23594 comment in `action-link-pages.ts` saying the notification surfaces were re-ruled here.
